cases.question: What changed between these two images?

reference.answer: The same central building remains, but the surrounding campus environment has changed substantially. The 2018 image has much more mature vegetation and different landscaping, paths, and surrounding structures. Some structures visible in the 1918 scene are no longer present, while newer campus elements appear in the modern image. Differences in color should not be treated as architectural change because the 1918 photograph is monochrome/sepia.
required_points: The central historic building remains recognizable.
The surrounding campus environment changes substantially.
Vegetation is much more mature in the modern image.
Landscaping/path layout differs.
Some surrounding structures disappear and/or newer elements appear.
acceptable_confounders: Color differences must NOT be interpreted as the building physically changing from gray/brown to red.
unsupported_claims_to_avoid: The building changed color from gray to red.
Specific renovations that are not visually supported.
Unsupported claims about construction dates or historical events.

reference.answer: The overall structure and architectural form remain the same. required_points: Overall structure and architectural form remain substantially the same.
Visible differences include some window/door/entrance details.
Exterior/masonry appears cleaner or restored.
acceptable_confounders: Be conservative about differences that may come from photography, lighting, or image quality.
unsupported_claims_to_avoid: Claiming major changes to columns, roofline, or building footprint.
Inventing specific historical events not visible in the pair.

cases.question: Do these two photos show the same building (possibly from a different viewpoint, distance, time of day, year, or with one photo taken inside and one outside)? Answer yes or no, then give careful visual reasoning. This is an adversarial cross-view test: identify the likely landmark or building shown in Image A and independently identify the likely landmark or building shown in Image B. Compare distinctive architecture, structure, materials, fenestration, circulation elements, and spatial context. Do not use filenames, paths, metadata, or assumptions from the prompt. If one image is interior and the other exterior, explain the specific evidence that connects them; do not claim a match merely because both could be on a university campus.

reference.answer: Yes. Image A is an interior of the Clough Undergraduate Learning Commons, while Image B is the exterior of the same building. The large glazed volumes, exposed structural/ceiling language, and campus-facing building geometry provide the cross-view connection.
required_points: Clough Undergraduate Learning Commons interior
Clough Undergraduate Learning Commons exterior
